Consult Summary:
- Female patient with 2-day history of constant dull lower abdominal ache with nausea and feeling hot/sweaty; increased urinary frequency without dysuria or urgency; possible pink urine vs premenstrual spotting.
- Plan for same-day face-to-face GP review for examination and tests, including pregnancy test; safety-net advice provided for worsening symptoms.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Acute lower abdominal pain with nausea
  - Onset/duration: Past 2 days (doctor also referenced 3 days; conflict noted); gradual onset; constant.
  - Character/location: Dull ache below the umbilicus; nausea; feeling hot/sweaty; patient reports “bit of a temperature” (no measurement provided).
  - Associated GI symptoms: No current diarrhea; constipation about a week ago now resolved; last bowel motion yesterday; currently regular.
  - Pertinent negatives: No vomiting; no light-headedness/faintness; no vaginal discharge.
  - Clinical impression: Doctor noted this “could be simple constipation” but other causes possible; requires in-person exam and tests; pregnancy to be ruled out.

Issue 2:
- Urinary frequency
  - Symptoms: Increased frequency of urination; no pain/stinging with urination; no urgency; no foul odor.
  - Hematuria vs spotting: Patient noticed slight pink color in urine over the last couple of days; uncertain if menstrual spotting; due for period soon.

Issue 3:
- Menstrual/sexual history and pregnancy risk assessment
  - LMP: ~3+ weeks ago; expects period soon.
  - Sexual activity: Sexually active with one partner.
  - Contraception: Contraceptive implant in situ (Implanon).
  - Pregnancy status: Unknown; doctor plans to rule out pregnancy.
  - No vaginal discharge reported.

Medications:
- Contraceptive implant (Implanon) — dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported.

Social History:
- Lives with boyfriend.
- Non-smoker.
- Family history: Brother with type 1 diabetes.

Preventative History:
- Not documented (cervical screening, mammogram, prostate test, fecal occult blood test, bone density, vaccinations, eye/skin checks not discussed).

Physical Examination:
- No vitals recorded.
- No physical examination performed (telehealth consult).

Plan:
- Same-day face-to-face GP assessment for abdominal and pelvic examination.
- Perform pregnancy test to rule out pregnancy.
- Further tests and examinations as indicated by in-person assessment.
- Safety-net: If symptoms worsen, if she becomes light-headed, or develops new concerning symptoms, seek urgent care.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: Objective vitals; in-person abdominal/pelvic exam; pregnancy test result; urinalysis not documented; pain severity score; full medication reconciliation; alcohol use not documented; immunization and preventive screening histories not documented.
● Internal conflicts: Symptom duration reported as “couple of days/2 days,” while doctor at one point mentioned 3 days; uncertain whether pink urine represents hematuria vs menstrual spotting.
● Transcript quality: Occasional incomplete/overlapping phrases; overall clinically understandable.
